title: This actually works
body:
I have tried lots of planners, but they always seem usable for a day or two, and then - the next thing you know - you realise that you haven’t used it for a week…

I had the version with the AI integration, and I think this is what makes it work so well. By asking it to create a task, you need to give it some details about the task itself… then you can ask it to create subtasks. <— this is where the magic happens. By breaking it down into potential tasks that are close enough to make you think about what they actually need to be, you end up properly planning the detailed steps and checking them off one by one. 

This has been massive for me. I’ve been using it for a month - for work tasks and basic everyday tasks and it’s a game changer. 

It’s especially great if your someone who humps from one task to another like I do. ADHDers, this one’s a dream!

title: Slick, well-priced, but not really helpful.
body:
This review is based on a short, few-days free trial. 

First I have to say that I love the notes widget. I almost paid for the app just for that. If it didn’t ‘vanish’ the objectives achieved one checked off, I probably would have. 

For the rest…. The UI is slick. Everything works smoothly and well. Unfortunately, it’s not really helpful. Here are the main reasons why: 

1: It doesn’t make noise at you to do the thing you’d planned to do. (My phone does spend most time on DND  to help prevent distractions - but all push notifications for this app were enabled. It made no difference. Also even when I saw a notification, it just assumes you’re doing it so it doesn’t bother you once it starts the timer.).

2: If you missed the thing you’d planned to do (aka not ticked it off at the end of the scheduled time) it doesn’t agitate at you to do it later that day in a free space. 

3: While it does offer ‘pause’ or ‘reschedule’, it doesn’t offer any kind of ‘not today’ or ‘chose not to do’ option. It might sound silly, but when I don’t go to scheduled work because of a public holiday or illness, I want the app to track it differently to something I just failed to motivate myself to do.

4: Want to create something similar but different? (For eg birthdays or second or third job schedules.) There’s no ‘duplicate’ option. Every single one must be created manually, even if you want the same reminders and checklists, just on different dates. 

5: AI-generated steps is a neat trick, but I often found it didn’t seem to understand what I was trying to achieve and I got caught in a bit of a loop for a while there trying to figure out what sort of task title would be ‘recognised’ enough for the AI checklist to work properly. Never actually figured that out. It’s cool, but not quite there yet. 

Very cool app, love how professional it feels, love LOVE the embedded notes app, but not really helpful for ADHD.

title: Don't get the lifetime subscription!
body:
I bought the lifetime subscription. Literally the day after I purchased it the app completely wiped itself, so I asked for a refund and it's been over a week and I haven't heard back from anyone! For the record, under Australian consumer laws I am entitled to a refund on any faulty product for up to a year after purchase! This company doesn't care about the people it supposedly wants to help! It only cares about taking your money!

Edit: just for the record, when I say I asked for a refund the email provided in the dev's response is exactly the method I used to contact the company (which as I said got no response)!

If the company was doing app maintenance, then I'm willing to give them another try (considering I still have almost a full year to still get a refund, and if the app ends up being helpful to me, then I want to use it), however there's no point providing me an email to contact for a refund when nobody from the company will respond to me through the proper communication methods!

Unless this company starts treating their customers better (regardless of whether I continue to stay with the app), my opinion remains the same as above! I shouldn't need to leave a public review to get recognition over a problem I'm having, and then be provided with what I expect is a completely useless email address, since that's how I was ignored in the first place!

Tiimo if you want people to support your company then treat ALL your customers with respect! Not just the customers who choose to stay with you! Afterall just because someone leaves, doesn't mean they aren't still willing to recommend you just because you might not have been the app they needed!

But I can promise you, considering my experiences here, I definitely won't be recommending you to anyone in the future! I don't feel like a respected and valued customer, I feel like I've been ignored and placated purely for the sake of your reputation, and NOT for the sake of you wanting to support your customers!

If you respect and support your customers, you'll make more money in the long run! That's just common sense!

title: Almost 5 stars
body:
I have autism and this is a great app for visually tracking time

Some suggestions. 

Editing event time is tricky. I change the finish time and it will alter the duration. This needs to be quicker. 

I have trouble estimating and planning out time over several days. It would be great to have projects with an estimated time and then as you schedule them out it adds up how much time you’ve allocated. That way I would be able to see if I have allocated enough time. 

Another suggestion would be grouping by categories or projects and then having some weekly stats. Eg to see how much time and percentage I have spent on leisure, work, fitness, down time each week. For example I have trouble planning out my week to fit in enough rest time, it would be great to be able to see that I planned out 4 hours or 5% down time this week but only got in 3 hours.

title: Life changing assistive technology
body:
Tiimo has been a central tool in my life for almost 2 years now. Having limited fine motor skills mean that paper planners aren’t an option for me, so executive dysfunction and my need for planning/routine was very difficult to meet previously. 

Being from Australia, currency conversion rates limit my access to neurodivergent-targeted assistive technology because it is often designed overseas. Considering how helpful Tiimo has been, I think it is excellent value for money. 

I was initially hesitant to commit to the subscription because I don’t generally use paid apps, and seeing reports of glitches and bugs furthered my wariness. I am so glad I ‘took a chance’ in this situation though, as Tiimo exceeded my expectations and has supported me through many major routine changes. It is a life changing piece of assistive technology in my life as an autistic+adhd young person.

I look forward to seeing how Tiimo develops in the future.

The response from the developers was basically unless you could record it happening (a recording not a screenshot) they didn’t seem overly interested or particularly concerned about the user experience. I have found an alternative app which is not quite as advanced but much less glitchy.

The Tiimo team have responded and none of that information they mentioned was communicated to me at the time. As someone with ADHD each glitch was a significant distraction, and the amount of mental effort it takes me to provide the feedback I did is quite high. Given neurological diverse people are your primary consumer it is super important to make sure people feel seen and heard.

body:
I really wanted to like Tiimo. This is the second time I’ve tried them and I signed up for a year thinking the bugs had been worked out. 

Takes ages to set up on the phone. Takes just as long, but is different setting up on computer. Slow process, slow to load, lots of double ups if you’re trying to reuse activities or worse, you inadvertently change the date or time for something in the future without realising. 

Finally get it set up, only to realise days later that I’m not getting notified. Nothing in my notifications history. I’ve got it all set in app and on phone to do them, but it just stops after a few days. App is still running in background. 

This keeps happening. Sometimes closing and reopening the app fixes it. Sometimes changing something fixes it. It shouldn’t be happening to begin with. I don’t have the spoons. 

I need those prompts but they just don’t happen with any reliability. 

This app would only work for me if I didn’t have ADHD.

title: Glasses for Time Blindness
body:
To get the most out of this app you need to understand the problem it’s solving. If you suffer with this problem, you’ll be more than happy to pay the subscription! (I think this is the reason for the poor ratings on this brilliant app).

If you have time blindness (look it up 🤓) + think more visually, and desperately want order in your life, this app is likely the answer.✅

People I see only occasionally have commented on how relaxed I seem 🏝. They all think I’m on holiday but it’s the result of not constantly chewing up all of my energy trying to keep an eye on my diary/calendar/clock, trying not to forget silly things like taking lunch to work (and still failing then stressing about it) and then being too exhausted to DO anything. 💤

I’ve tried SO many organisational systems 🗂 over the years and my inability to keep them going has left me feeling a bit lower each time. Using those tools only was like being taught how to focus on things by someone with 20/20 vision while everything is just blurry to me. Now that I have glasses (Tiimo) 👓 some of those systems may actually be useful! 

THANK YOU Tiimo team! 🍻

P.S. I’m normally too lazy/disorganised/in energy-conservation-mode to write these but made the effort this time because if all I have to do to help someone else in my situation get the results I have is write this then that’s a massive result to energy ratio and worth the trouble.
